Lots of retrospectives start with a prompt that focuses on "problems". What is broken? Where did we mess up during the last sprint?

A different approach is to brainstorm opportunities. Don't linger on what's broken.

This prompts might help...

employers struggling to find "talent" should start advertising things like:

-No story points
-No fake deadlines
-3d turnaround to request new machines
-We use (tooling) to make your life easier
-CI/CD performance
-Team rotation to learn new things
-Mgrs who have done this before

I'm worried

That there's too much focus on things like "mindset", "empowerment", "leadership", etc.

And too little focus on the "boring" parts of making our working setups more sane, reducing cognitive overhead, and decoupling where it makes sense

The former burns people out

product management super-skill

➕time and energy on high value certainty and uncertainty

➖time and energy on low value certainty and uncertainty

here's a big problem with companies adopting OKRs (and frankly companies that have been using them for a while...)

there's a lack of clarify about the WHY

WHY are you using OKRs?

What do you hope to see more of / less of?

Good activity...

A big lesson I've learned over the last couple years

Some % of ppl love A but if you stop there, most ppl will get overwhelmed

Teams have a tendency to jump to C ... but your most passionate problem solvers will spin their wheels

B is the "right way" ... but the hardest work
